lesson.title: A picture is a grid of numbers
lesson.subtitle: A filter mixes neighbours

video.title: A picture is a grid of numbers: A filter mixes neighbours
video.format_note: Animated explainer, 16:9, flat Darsi colours. Narration in the lesson language. Captions are separate files.
cast: Joseph - computer studies teacher, talking to a fellow lecturer
Narrator - the Darsi voice, warm and precise, talking to a university lecturer

scenes.narration: Students say the filter sees a door. Make them point at the nine multiplications. The door is their name for a pattern of edges.
In the seminar: a grid, nine multiplications, and a stop before any photo of a person.
A grey image is one grid. A colour image is three, and each cell is a brightness, not an object.
A three by three filter lays on the picture and multiplies nine cells. It writes that sum as the new pixel.
An upright-edge filter lights walls. A blur averages neighbours, and neither knows it is looking at a face.
Here is one position of the filter. Nine multiplications become one number, and the name of the object is not in that number.
Quick check! A grey picture on a computer is which of these?
A grid of numbers. Names, if they appear, come from many layers, not from one filter.
Pairs say the nine-term sum out loud once before they run the filter on the whole picture. Drawn edges are enough.
Your turn. Does a three by three filter already know it is looking at a face?
Remember this. A filter mixes neighbours. It does not name what it sees.
Try it in your next lecture. Collect the sentence it knows it is a door, and answer it with the nine multiplications.

checkpoints.prompt: A grey picture on a computer is which of these?

options.text: One bit for the whole photo

checkpoints.feedback_correct: Correct: each cell is a brightness. Colour is three such grids.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite: a grey picture is a grid of numbers.

checkpoints.prompt: Does a three by three filter already know it is looking at a face?

options.text: Only if the picture is a photo

checkpoints.feedback_correct: Correct: it multiplies nine cells. It does not know a name.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite: a small filter only mixes neighbours.
